standing_rule: these are VALIDATIONS, not calibrations.  No value in the chain was tuned toward any of them.  A disagreement becomes an issue in PROJECT_TRACE section 9; it is never a reason to move a number.

literature.reference: Harer, Vieu, Schulze, Larkin & Reville 2025, A&A 703, A111
literature.method: Hoki (Stevance et al. 2020) interface to BPASS (Stanway & Eldridge 2018)
literature.text_verbatim: For an age of 3-5 Myr, type Ic supernovae are by far the most likely type of supernova, and the rate is consistent with several supernovae per Myr.
literature.unit_trap: the axis is events per 100 kiloyears, NOT per 100 years.  1 event/100 kyr = 10 SNe/Myr; 1 event/100 yr would be 10,000 SNe/Myr.  Misreading it inflates the expected rate by a factor of 1000.

harer_2025.our_estimator: dN_SN/dt = k * M_turnoff^(-alpha) * |dM_turnoff/dt|, summed over subgroups; cumulative = k * integral[M_turnoff, 120] dM M^-alpha.  Association mass = k * integral[0.5, 120] dM M^(1-alpha).

matched_alpha_comparison.note: compared at THEIR assumed alpha, which is our shallow branch, not our baseline

cumulative_vs_rate_reconciliation.explanation: the PARSEC turnoff only falls below the 120 Msun IMF ceiling at 2.99 Myr, so no star could have exploded before then.  CygOB2-A is 3.98 Myr old, giving a supernova window of about 1 Myr; a cumulative count of ~6 and a rate of ~8/Myr are the same statement, not a contradiction.
cumulative_vs_rate_reconciliation.CygOB2_C_contributes_zero: at 2.51 Myr its turnoff is still above the IMF upper limit — nothing has died there yet

harer_2025.mass_caveat: the association mass is sensitive to the low-mass integration limit.  We integrate from 0.5 Msun, the frozen MASS_GRID edge; a single alpha=2.3 power law continued to 0.1 Msun would give 3.1e4 Msun.  The real IMF flattens below ~0.5 Msun, so our cutoff happens to mimic a Kroupa turnover.  Good agreement, but not to be quoted better than a few tens of percent.
harer_2025.physical_difference_carried: BPASS models binary evolution and their Fig. 2 shows type Ic dominating at 3-5 Myr — the stripped-envelope channel, which REQUIRES a companion.  Our count is single-star turnoff counting.  Our N_SN is therefore a LOWER BOUND relative to a BPASS-style rate, and we agree with them before adding that channel.  Same physics as issue #15, from another direction.

literature.zero_point: DR2 global offset -0.029 mas (Lindegren et al. 2018)

orellana_2021.pm_significance: pmra agrees to 0.003 mas/yr against an independent DR2 analysis, which directly validates the issue #16 fix: the vector the runaway traceback subtracts is externally confirmed.  The 0.077 mas/yr pmdec difference is 0.59 km/s at 1.62 kpc, negligible against a 10-100 km/s ejection window.
orellana_2021.distance_offset_cause: parallax zero point.  They apply the DR2 global -0.029 mas (Lindegren et al. 2018); we apply the DR3 per-star Lindegren et al. 2021 correction.  Their mean member parallax is 0.599 mas, ours 0.614 — the 0.015 mas difference is the scale of a DR2 to DR3 zero-point revision.

propagated_systematic.direction: adopting their distance raises every closure ratio by about 2%: it HELPS CygOB2-A (0.894, below unity) and HURTS CygOB2-C (1.405)
propagated_systematic.not_adopted: changing the distance to match a cross-check would be tuning.  Recorded as a systematic instead.

orellana_2021.verdict: AGREE on proper motion; 3% distance offset carried as a systematic

literature.reference: Berlanas, Wright, Herrero, Drew & Lennon 2019, MNRAS 484, 1838
literature.claim: line-of-sight substructure: main group ~1760 pc, foreground ~1350 pc

berlanas_2019.CIRCULARITY_CAVEAT: WP2's membership classifier uses FEATURES = ['parallax_corrected', 'pmra', 'pmdec'] — PARALLAX IS A CLUSTERING FEATURE.  A foreground group at 1350 pc would have been assigned low membership probability and removed BEFORE this test ran.  The honest scope is therefore: 'within the WP2 member sample there is no evidence of two distances'.  It is NOT evidence against Berlanas's foreground group.
berlanas_2019.what_would_settle_it: a test on a PARALLAX-BLIND selection — members chosen on sky position and proper motion only, then examined in parallax.  Not done here; it is the only way to break the circularity.
berlanas_2019.corroboration: Orellana et al. 2021 independently find foreground structure in the same field: 179 and 188 stars at ~1280 pc plus UCB585 at ~1460 pc, all with proper motions distinct from Cyg OB2.  All three analyses agree that foreground structure EXISTS and is separable by proper motion; the disagreement is about whether those stars are Cyg OB2 members, not whether they are there.
berlanas_2019.open_question_for_wp6: a star truly at 1350 pc but assumed at 1620 gets a distance modulus 0.40 mag too large, so it is inferred MORE massive, which INFLATES the count above 8 Msun and RAISES the closure ratio — the direction of CygOB2-C's 1.405 residual.  Our data do not support it (C's foreground fraction matches A and B, and no member sits at 1350 pc), but note that WP6 alternative A4 tested membership-probability weighting, NOT distance contamination.  This mechanism is covered by no WP6 alternative and is registered as open.
berlanas_2019.verdict: NOT CONFIRMED — but this test cannot settle the claim
